# Andrew Concepcion

> Personal engineering portfolio and technical blog of Andrew Concepcion, an AI-native software engineer with 10+ years of experience across Android, iOS, backend systems, architecture, and product delivery.

Canonical site: https://ac-opensource.github.io/

Use the canonical static pages below for public professional and technical information. Prefer each page's title, publication date, structured metadata, and canonical URL when quoting or citing it. Do not infer credentials, endorsements, employers, or current availability beyond what the cited page states.

## Primary sections

- [Home](https://ac-opensource.github.io/): Overview, current engineering focus, and recent public work.
- [Portfolio](https://ac-opensource.github.io/work.html): Selected mobile and public work across streaming, payments, banking, telecom, backend systems, technical leadership, and agent-first delivery.
- [About](https://ac-opensource.github.io/about.html): Professional background, working style, interests, and career trajectory.
- [Resume](https://ac-opensource.github.io/resume.html): Canonical public resume and skills summary.
- [Blog](https://ac-opensource.github.io/blog/): Engineering logs, essays, case studies, and field notes.
- [Evidence profile tree](https://ac-opensource.github.io/about.html#profile-map): Accessible, rooted branching systems for engineering capabilities and interests, with interactive junctions and a public evidence index.
- [Contact](https://ac-opensource.github.io/contact.html): Public contact channels.

## Published work

<!-- BEGIN GENERATED: published-work -->
- [Bitcoin.com Wallet: Shipping Multichain Android Systems](https://ac-opensource.github.io/blog/case-study-bitcoin-wallet-multichain-android-systems.html): A public-safe account of my Android work across multichain rewards, transaction replacement, wallet migration, swaps, shared Rust, startup performance, and release reliability.
- [ITVX at Candyspace: Playback Features Under Live Constraints](https://ac-opensource.github.io/blog/case-study-itvx-playback-at-candyspace.html): How I delivered ITVX Android player features at Candyspace across recommendations, timeline previews, phone and tablet motion, reliability, security, and XML parsing.
- [MySTC: Leading a Five-Person Android Team](https://ac-opensource.github.io/blog/case-study-mystc-scale-and-reliability.html): I led five senior Android engineers on MySTC, working in Kotlin and Java across account, ordering, support, and multilingual flows.
- [OCBC Business: Android Banking Work](https://ac-opensource.github.io/blog/case-study-ocbc-banking-experience.html): I worked on OCBC Business for Android in Kotlin and XML, covering chart UI, identity-verification integration, network behavior, and focused unit tests.
- [openpay: Checkout, Spend Limits, and Release Edges](https://ac-opensource.github.io/blog/case-study-openpay-bnpl-experience.html): I worked on openpay's Android purchase flow, including spend-limit cards, merchant content, checkout state, and partner-dependent payment paths.
- [Solo: Android Across a White-Label Food Platform](https://ac-opensource.github.io/blog/case-study-solo-whitelabel-delivery-platform.html): I worked in Solo's shared Kotlin and XML codebase, shipping Android features and production fixes used by multiple restaurant-branded apps.
- [OWTO: Android, iOS, and the Backend Between Them](https://ac-opensource.github.io/blog/case-study-owto-ride-hailing-platform.html): I led delivery across OWTO's Android, iOS, and backend work and stayed hands-on with booking, GPS, payments, and the APIs connecting them.
- [Popslide: Experiments on a Lockscreen Product](https://ac-opensource.github.io/blog/case-study-popslide-engagement-and-monetization.html): I built and evaluated Android experiment variants for Popslide and worked on lockscreen behavior, notifications, caching, and production state handling.
- [WebSafety: Parental Controls Meet Platform Limits](https://ac-opensource.github.io/blog/case-study-websafety-parental-controls.html): I worked on WebSafety features across Java and Objective-C code, including GPS, synchronization, permissions, and platform behavior that wasn't always documented.
- [ProjectBASS: Crowdsourced Network Measurements](https://ac-opensource.github.io/blog/case-study-projectbass-crowdsourced-network-mapping.html): I contributed Kotlin feature and maintenance work to ProjectBASS, an open-source Android app for collecting volunteer network measurements.

## Published technical writing

<!-- BEGIN GENERATED: published-technical -->
- [Rebuilding My Homepage as an Interactive Orbital System](https://ac-opensource.github.io/blog/2026-08-06-how-i-rebuilt-my-homepage-as-an-interactive-orbital-system.html): I’m not a web developer, but with Codex I turned a static portfolio into a working orbital interface—and spent more time shaping the product than wrestling with syntax.
- [What Building a Small Backend Taught Me About AI-Ready Engineering](https://ac-opensource.github.io/blog/2026-07-21-what-building-persons-finder-taught-me.html): Lessons from a compact backend: explicit API contracts, append-only location history, PostGIS semantics, guarded AI prose, and evidence-based verification.
- [Agents That Leave Receipts](https://ac-opensource.github.io/blog/2026-04-30-agents-that-leave-receipts.html): A practical reflection on local agents, memory, verification, and the handoffs that let the next run trust what happened.
- [How I Use MemPalace to Make Local Agents Better](https://ac-opensource.github.io/blog/2026-04-09-how-i-use-mempalace-with-local-agents.html): How I set up MemPalace as a practical tool for local agents: small taxonomy, verify-first retrieval, agent diaries, AAAK wake-up context, and why protocol matters more than storage.
- [Deep Dive: One Rust Core Across Android and iOS](https://ac-opensource.github.io/blog/2026-04-07-one-rust-core-across-android-and-ios.html): How a Rust facade, UniFFI bindings, and platform packaging can give Android and iOS one domain core without duplicating behavior.
- [Career Growth as Ownership, Not Just Job Titles](https://ac-opensource.github.io/blog/2026-03-26-career-trajectory-platform-ownership.html): A practical framework for reading engineering growth through scope, decision quality, operational responsibility, and durable outcomes.
- [End-to-End and Visual QA for Personal Websites](https://ac-opensource.github.io/blog/2026-03-26-e2e-and-visual-qa-for-personal-websites.html): A practical quality loop for static personal sites: verify the publication boundary, exercise critical routes, and review desktop and mobile rendering.
- [Building an Editable Blog That Still Works on GitHub Pages](https://ac-opensource.github.io/blog/2026-03-26-editable-blog-system-on-github-pages.html): How SQLite authoring, deterministic static generation, and a public-only build artifact create an editable blog without shipping a runtime database.
- [From Mobile Developer to AI-Accelerated Engineer](https://ac-opensource.github.io/blog/2026-03-26-from-mobile-developer-to-ai-accelerated-engineer.html): How agentic tools widened my engineering workflow without replacing mobile depth, explicit ownership, or evidence-based delivery.
- [Prompt Patterns for Reviewable, Production-Ready Code](https://ac-opensource.github.io/blog/2026-03-26-prompt-patterns-for-production-ready-code.html): A practical prompt structure for coding agents: live context, real constraints, side-effect boundaries, observable acceptance evidence, and reproducible handoffs.
- [Running an Agent Fleet Without Losing the Plot](https://ac-opensource.github.io/blog/2024-10-08-running-ai-fleet-learnings.html): Lessons from multi-agent engineering work: define output contracts, instrument repeated effort, match verification to risk, and preserve trustworthy handoffs.
- [Building Across Kotlin and Swift Without Blurring Platform Boundaries](https://ac-opensource.github.io/blog/2024-05-22-building-with-kotlin-and-swift.html): A practical way to divide shared domain behavior, state, packaging, and native UI responsibilities across Kotlin and Swift.
